_help: Each paragraph is a list of segments. A plain string is read by the narrator and split into sentences automatically. A one-key object like {"Pip": "text"} is dialogue read with that character's voice. After editing, run: .venv/bin/python tools/generate_audio.py

summary.es: Un zorrito y sus amigos animales del bosque ayudan a una estrella caída a volver al cielo.
summary.en: A little fox and his animal friends from the forest help a fallen star get back to the sky.

chapters.title: The Star in the Meadow
paragraphs: Once upon a time, at the edge of a quiet forest, there lived a little fox named Pip. Pip had a fluffy orange tail and lots of animal friends.
One night, everyone was asleep. The rabbits were asleep in their burrow. The mice were asleep under the roots. Even the birds were asleep in their nests.
But Pip could not sleep. He peeked out of his den and saw a tiny light falling from the sky. It landed softly in the meadow, next to the pond.
Pip tiptoed through the grass. A green frog jumped onto a lily pad.
There, between two daisies, was a little star. She was glowing, but only a tiny bit. And she was crying.
whispered Pip.

paragraphs.Pip: “I'm Pip, the fox. Are you okay?”

paragraphs: sniffled the star.

paragraphs.Twinkle: “My name is Twinkle. I was playing tag with the moon, and I slipped. Now I can't get home.”

paragraphs: A sleepy rabbit hopped over. A little mouse came too. They all looked up at the sky. It was very, very far away.
said Pip.

paragraphs.Pip: “My friends and I will help you get home. I promise.”

paragraphs: Twinkle smiled, and her light grew a little bit brighter.

chapters.title: The Tallest Hill

paragraphs.Twinkle: “Where is the closest place to the sky?”

paragraphs: asked Twinkle.
Pip thought and thought.

paragraphs.Pip: “Grandpa Owl will know! Owls are very wise.”

paragraphs: So Pip carried Twinkle to the oldest tree in the forest. A squirrel ran down the trunk to say hello. High on a branch sat Grandpa Owl, blinking his big yellow eyes.

paragraphs.Owl: “Hoo, hoo. Climb the Tallest Hill, little fox. At the top, the sky is close enough to touch. But first, you must cross the river.”

paragraphs: At the river, a family of ducks was swimming. Quack, quack! Silver fish jumped out of the water. Splash!
asked Pip.
A busy beaver pushed a big log across the water. Now there was a bridge!
On the other side, they met a big brown bear eating berries.
said the bear, pointing with his paw.
Pip's legs were tired, but he did not stop.
said Twinkle.
said Pip. And step by step, they climbed higher and higher.

chapters.title: Home in the Sky
paragraphs: At last, Pip reached the top of the Tallest Hill. The stars looked so close!
But Twinkle was worried.

paragraphs.Twinkle: “I'm too dim to fly. How will I get back up there?”

paragraphs: Pip had an idea.

paragraphs.Pip: “Maybe you need to feel happy to shine bright!”

paragraphs: Just then, all of Pip's friends arrived. The rabbit, the mouse, and the frog. The squirrel, the ducks, and the big brown bear. Even a gentle deer and Grandpa Owl came to help.
The frog did a funny dance. Ribbit, ribbit! The ducks sang a silly song. Quack, quack! The bear told a joke about honey.
Everyone laughed and laughed. And with every laugh, Twinkle glowed brighter. And brighter. And brighter!
Slowly, Twinkle began to float.
Up, up, up she flew, until she found her place in the sky.
The animals cheered. Then one little star winked at them. Twice.
And every night after that, before he went to sleep, Pip looked up and winked back.
The End.

summary.es: Una nube pequeñita viaja sobre montañas, ríos y lagos, y descubre su propia manera de ayudar.
summary.en: A tiny cloud travels over mountains, rivers and lakes, and discovers his very own way to help.

chapters.title: Too Small to Rain
paragraphs: High in the blue sky, above the mountains and the forest, lived a little cloud named Nimbus.
Below him, Nimbus could see everything. Tall green trees. A long, shiny river. Fields of grass and flowers. And the warm, yellow sun smiling over it all.
Every morning, the big clouds gathered over the mountains. They grew dark and heavy, and then, splish, splash, they made rain for the forest and the fields.
asked Nimbus.
Mama Cumulus, the biggest cloud of all, smiled kindly.

paragraphs.Mama: “Of course you can, little one. Try!”

paragraphs: Nimbus squeezed and squeezed. He puffed up his cheeks. But nothing happened. Not a single raindrop.
he said sadly.

paragraphs.Mama: “Being small is not the same as being no good,”

paragraphs: said Mama Cumulus.

paragraphs.Mama: “Everyone has their own way to help.”

paragraphs: Just then, the wind blew softly.

paragraphs.Wind: “Come with me, little cloud. I will show you the world.”

paragraphs: So Nimbus floated away on the wind, wondering what a little cloud could do.

chapters.title: The Thirsty Garden
paragraphs: The wind carried Nimbus over a tall mountain with snow on top. They passed a deep blue lake and a quiet valley full of rocks.
At last, Nimbus saw a tiny garden next to a little yellow house.
The garden looked very sad. The soil was dry and cracked. The grass was brown. The leaves on the little tree were crunchy. And in the middle stood one small daisy, bending her head toward the ground.
called Nimbus.
sighed the daisy.

paragraphs.Daisy: “The big clouds never come here. Our garden is too small for them to notice.”

paragraphs: Too small to notice. Nimbus knew exactly how that felt.
he said.
So Nimbus floated right over the garden. His soft, round body made a cool, gentle shadow. The flowers stopped wilting. The daisy lifted her head.
she said.
Nimbus felt a warm, happy feeling inside.

chapters.title: Nimbus Shines
paragraphs: Nimbus stayed with the garden all afternoon. He told the daisy about mountains, lakes, and rivers. The daisy told him about seeds, roots, and bees.
Nimbus was so happy that he felt full. Full of joy, full of friendship, full of something tingly.
Then, plip! A single raindrop fell from Nimbus and landed on the daisy's petal.
gasped Nimbus.
Plip, plop, plip! Gentle rain began to fall. The dry soil drank and drank. The brown grass turned green. New leaves grew on the little tree.
cheered the daisy.
When the rain stopped, the sun peeked out. Its light shone through the last raindrops, and a beautiful rainbow appeared over the garden. Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple!
That evening, the wind carried Nimbus home over the mountains.

paragraphs.Nimbus: “Mama, I found my way to help! Small clouds can make small rain for small gardens.”

paragraphs: Mama Cumulus gave him a big, fluffy hug.
And from that day on, whenever a little garden felt thirsty, Nimbus was always the first to come.
The End.

summary.es: Un conejito siembra un jardín de frutas y aprende que lo bueno toma tiempo y es mejor compartido.
summary.en: A bunny plants a fruit garden and learns that good things take time and are better shared.

chapters.title: The Tiny Seeds
paragraphs: Benny was a bunny with long floppy ears and a very big dream. He wanted to grow a garden full of fruit.
One sunny morning, Grandma Bunny gave him a little paper bag.

paragraphs.Grandma: “These are fruit seeds, Benny. Take good care of them.”

paragraphs: Benny looked inside. There were tiny apple seeds and round cherry pits. There were flat watermelon seeds and little strawberry plants. There was even a baby lemon tree!
shouted Benny.

paragraphs.Benny: “Today I will plant my fruit garden!”

paragraphs: He dug little holes with his paws. He planted the seeds one by one. He watered them with his tiny blue watering can.
Then Benny sat down and waited. And waited. And waited.
His friend Tilly the turtle came walking by, very slowly.

paragraphs.Benny: “I'm waiting for my apples and strawberries,”

paragraphs: said Benny.

paragraphs.Benny: “They should be ready any minute now.”

paragraphs: Tilly smiled a slow, wise smile.

paragraphs.Tilly: “Fruit doesn't grow in minutes, Benny. It grows in weeks and months. Good things take time.”

paragraphs: Benny's ears drooped. Weeks? Months? That sounded like forever.

chapters.title: Waiting Is Hard
paragraphs: The next morning, Benny ran outside. No apples. No strawberries. Just brown dirt.
Milo the mouse peeked out from under a leaf. He was eating a handful of blueberries.

paragraphs.Milo: “Benny, why do you look so grumpy?”

paragraphs: said Benny.

paragraphs.Benny: “I want a big red apple now!”

paragraphs: said Milo.

paragraphs.Milo: “When I'm waiting for something, I keep busy. Why don't you take care of your garden while it grows?”

paragraphs: So Benny tried. Every day, he watered the soil. He pulled out the weeds. He shooed away the hungry crows. And while he worked, he forgot to be grumpy.
One morning, Benny saw tiny green sprouts. Then he saw little white flowers on the strawberry plants. Then a tiny green bump appeared on the lemon tree!
asked Benny, hopping in circles.
Tilly the turtle nodded.

paragraphs.Tilly: “You see? Waiting is hard. But when your paws are busy, it gets a little easier.”

chapters.title: A Fruit Picnic
paragraphs: Months went by, and Benny's garden grew and grew. There were sweet red strawberries and shiny red cherries. There were crunchy green apples and juicy pears. A big striped watermelon sat in the sun, and the lemon tree was full of yellow lemons.
Benny was so proud. But when he looked at all that fruit, he had a funny feeling.

paragraphs.Benny: “This is too much fruit for just one bunny,”

paragraphs: he said.
Then he remembered. Grandma had given him the seeds. Tilly had given him good advice. Milo had shared his blueberries.
said Benny.

paragraphs.Benny: “I will have a fruit picnic for everyone!”

paragraphs: On Saturday, all his friends came. Tilly brought a basket of oranges. Milo brought grapes and bananas. Grandma Bunny brought a pitcher of pink lemonade.
Together, they made the biggest fruit salad in the valley. Apples, pears, cherries, strawberries, oranges, grapes, and bananas, all in one bowl!
They ate cold slices of watermelon and laughed until the stars came out.
said Milo, with a very full tummy,
Benny smiled. It was not the best garden because it was big. It was the best garden because it was a garden for everyone.
The End.
